lines.trans: Morning, everyone! Mazen told me at the gate that you dug up buried treasure!
Better than gold coins, Ziad—look at this cream kitchen card from the tin!
Summer Berry and Almond Courtyard Cake—written in neat blue fountain pen!
Two hundred grams of ground almonds, soft butter, three eggs, and fresh summer berries...
Why did you stop reading at the best part, Salma?
Because someone tore the recipe card cleanly in half right across the middle!
Turn the half card over, my dear—there is a pencilled note on the back.
Read it aloud, Salma! Where did they hide the baking time and the glaze?

words.gloss: read it (feminine imperative, referring to feminine object)

lines.trans: Half in the tin, half pressed inside our favourite green book of garden leaves!

words.gloss: in the box / in the can

lines.trans: A recipe split into two halves like a treasure map—who bakes like that?!
Two clever friends who wanted us to search both the courtyard and the bookshelves!
Until we find that green leaf book, nobody gets a single slice of berry cake!

lines.trans: A recipe split into two halves like a treasure map—who bakes like that?!
Two clever friends who wanted us to search both the courtyard and the bookshelves!
Until we find that green leaf book, nobody gets a single slice of berry cake!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Elative form of حسن (hasan), used for comparison.

examples.trans: This is better than that.

examples.text: صحتي صارت أحسن بكتير بعد ما ارتحت يومين.
examples.trans: My health got much better after I rested for two days.

meanings.note: Elative of حلو (ḥilu), used for pretty, sweet, or nice.

examples.trans: This is the prettiest car I've seen.

examples.text: القهوة بدون سكر أحلى مع التمر.
examples.trans: Unsweetened coffee is nicer alongside dates.

meanings.note: Plural of ذكي (ḏakī).

examples.trans: The students in this class are very smart.

examples.text: الأولاد بالمدرسة أذكياء وبفهموا الدرس بسرعة.
examples.trans: The kids at school are bright and grasp the lesson quickly.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The color of my car is blue.

examples.text: السما اليوم لونها أزرق صافي وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky today is a clear blue and there are no clouds.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for seeing a group of people.

examples.trans: I will see you tomorrow at school.

examples.text: يلا مع السلامة، أشوفكم الأسبوع الجاي إن شاء الله.
examples.trans: Alright, goodbye—see you all next week, God willing.

meanings.note: إن (that) + كم (you plural).

examples.trans: I heard that you (all) are traveling.

examples.text: مبسوط إنكم جيتوا تزورونا بعطلة نهاية الأسبوع.
examples.trans: I'm glad that you all came to visit us over the weekend.

meanings.note: Independent object pronoun for the first person plural. Rare in spoken, mostly formal or specific expressions.

examples.trans: May God protect us and you.

examples.text: ربنا يحفظ إيانا وإياكم من كل سوء.
examples.trans: May God protect both us and you from every harm.

اقرئيها.gloss: read it (feminine imperative, referring to feminine object)

meanings.en: read it (feminine imperative, referring to feminine object)
meanings.note: Command to a female to read a feminine object (like a story or paper).

examples.trans: Take the letter and read it.

examples.text: الجريدة وصلت الصبح، اقرئيها وأنتِ بتشربي القهوة.
examples.trans: The newspaper arrived this morning—read it while you drink your coffee.

meanings.note: Command to a female to flip something.

examples.trans: Turn the page so I can see.

examples.text: اقلبي الرغيف عالجهة التانية عشان يتحمّر منيح.
examples.trans: Flip the loaf to the other side so it browns nicely.

meanings.note: The color green with the definite article.

examples.trans: The green line means go.

examples.text: الشاي الأخضر مع النعنع خفيف ومنعش بعد الغدا.
examples.trans: Green tea with mint is light and refreshing after lunch.

meanings.note: Refers to a large gate or portal, physical or digital.

examples.trans: Wait for me at the main gate.

examples.text: تلاقينا قدام البوابة الغربية للجامعة الساعة عشرة.
examples.trans: We met in front of the university's west gate at ten o'clock.

meanings.note: Commonly refers to mulberries, which are popular in Jordan, or any berry.

examples.trans: Mulberry juice is very delicious in the summer.

examples.text: شجرة التوت بالحديقة صارت مليانة حبات سودة حلوة.
examples.trans: The mulberry tree in the garden is full of sweet dark berries now.

meanings.note: The staple food in Jordan, often a symbol of livelihood.

examples.trans: I bought the bread from the bakery in the morning.

examples.text: ريحة الخبز السخن طالعة من الفرن على الشارع.
examples.trans: The smell of warm bread is wafting out of the bakery onto the street.

meanings.note: Goodness, kindness, or general prosperity/wealth.

examples.text: يعطيك ألف عافية، كتر الله من الخير.
examples.trans: May God give you health, may God increase the good/wealth.

examples.text: إن شاء الله السنة الجديدة بتجيب الخير للجميع.
examples.trans: Hopefully the new year brings goodness and blessings to everyone.

meanings.note: Precious metal, culturally significant for weddings in Jordan.

examples.trans: They bought the gold for my brother's engagement.

examples.text: أسعار الذهب طلعت هالأيام بسوق الصاغة.
examples.trans: Gold prices went up these days in the goldsmiths' market.

meanings.note: A concatenated corpus error, likely merging 'the square/arena' and 'written'.

examples.text: قصة الساحة مكتوبة في كتب التاريخ.
examples.trans: The story of the square is written in history books.

examples.text: كانت يافطة الساحة مكتوبة بخط واضح وكبير.
examples.trans: The plaza's sign was written in clear, large lettering.

meanings.note: Collective noun for trees.

examples.trans: The trees in the garden are beautiful.

examples.text: ورق الشجر بلش يصفر ويوقع بشهر تشرين.
examples.trans: The tree leaves started turning yellow and falling in October.

meanings.note: Relating to the summer.

examples.trans: I bought the summer clothes.

examples.text: الشمس بتحرق بالجو الصيفي بنص النهار.
examples.trans: The sun burns in the summer weather at midday.

meanings.note: General word for a small box, tin, or can.

examples.trans: Where is the empty box?

examples.text: خبي البسكوت جوا العلبة المسكرة عشان ما يطرا.
examples.trans: Keep the biscuits inside the sealed box so they don't go soft.

meanings.note: Plural of book.

examples.trans: Put the books in the bag.

examples.text: رتبت كل الكتب على الرف حسب التخصص.
examples.trans: I arranged all the books on the shelf by subject.

meanings.note: Used for food textures or colors (off-white).

examples.trans: The creamy soup is delicious.

examples.text: الصلصة الكريمية مع الباستا طلعت طعمها خيالي.
examples.trans: The creamy sauce with the pasta turned out tasting amazing.

meanings.note: Likely a typographical error or compound (e.g. whose treasure). Treated here as an odd plural/dual or typo.

examples.trans: The treasures (or sweaters) are unknown.

examples.text: سألت الشباب عن الكنزمين بس ولا واحد عرف معناها.
examples.trans: I asked the guys about that odd word, yet not one of them knew what it meant.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Standard word for kitchen.

examples.trans: The kitchen is clean today.

examples.text: أمي واقفة في المطبخ بتجهز الأكل للضيوف.
examples.trans: My mom is standing in the kitchen preparing food for the guests.

meanings.note: Favorite (masculine).

examples.trans: This is my favorite restaurant.

examples.text: المقلوبة هي الطبق المفضل عندي يوم الجمعة.
examples.trans: Maqluba is my favorite dish on Fridays.

meanings.note: Paper or leaves (collective).

examples.text: جيب معك شوية الورق عشان نكتب.
examples.trans: Bring some paper with you so we can write.

examples.text: خلص الورق من الطابعة ولازم نجيب رزمة جديدة.
examples.trans: The printer ran out of paper and we need to get a new ream.

meanings.note: Recipe or medical prescription.

examples.trans: This recipe for making knafeh is wonderful.

examples.text: أعطاني الصيدلاني الدوا حسب الوصفة اللي كتبها الدكتور.
examples.trans: The pharmacist gave me the medicine according to the prescription the doctor wrote.

meanings.note: In the courtyard, yard, or public square.

examples.trans: The boys are playing in the yard.
We drank tea in the courtyard under the tree.

meanings.note: Exactly, precisely.

examples.text: هذا اللي كنت بدي أحكيه بالضبط.
examples.trans: This is exactly what I wanted to say.
We arrived at nine o'clock sharp.

بالعلبة.gloss: in the box / in the can

meanings.en: in the box / in the can
meanings.note: In the box or the can.

examples.trans: The items are still in the box.
We found the square cards in the metal tin.

meanings.note: Used to indicate the center of something or splitting something equally.

examples.trans: Split the apple in half.
Tin Two is placed right in the middle.

meanings.note: Refers to writing or drawing done specifically using ink rather than a pencil.

examples.trans: I signed the paper with blue ink.

examples.text: العنوان مكتوب بحبر أزرق غامق على المغلف.
examples.trans: The address is written in dark blue ink on the envelope.

meanings.note: The most common way to express 'they want' in Jordanian and Palestinian dialects.

examples.trans: They want to go to the cinema.

examples.text: الضيوف بدهم يذوقوا الكيكة التالتة كمان.
examples.trans: The guests want to taste the third cake as well.

meanings.note: Refers to vocalization, often used in phrases like 'b-ṣōt ʿālī' (with a loud voice).

examples.trans: Don't speak with a loud voice.

examples.text: قرأ الرسالة بصوت واطي عشان ما حدا يسمع.
examples.trans: He read the letter in a low voice so no one would hear.

meanings.note: Singular form for any type of card (ID, credit, ticket, etc.).

examples.trans: My bank card is lost.

examples.text: كل بطاقة عليها رقم ورمز مرسوم بالحبر.
examples.trans: Each card has a number and a symbol drawn in ink.

meanings.note: Used to indicate authorship or the instrument used.

examples.trans: This article is by a famous writer.

examples.text: سلمى سجلت النتايج بقلم رصاص ناعم.
examples.trans: Salma recorded the results with a soft pencil.

meanings.note: Used in Levantine dialects to mean "like this" or "with this kind of".

examples.trans: In such a case, we must be careful.

examples.text: بهيك حالة لازم نعيد قراءة التعليمات.
examples.trans: In such a case we need to re-read the instructions.

meanings.note: Describes the action of baking bread or pastries.

examples.text: هو بيخبز خبز طازج كل الصبح.
examples.trans: He bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: الفران بيخبز الخبز الطازج قبل الفجر.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread before dawn.

meanings.note: Plural form of egg, commonly used when counting eggs.

examples.trans: I bought five eggs from the shop.

examples.text: استعملنا تلات بيضات طازجة للكيكة الإسفنجية.
examples.trans: We used three fresh eggs for the sponge cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: The feminine form of the Levantine possessive marker.

examples.trans: Reem's bag is lost.

examples.text: العلبة تبعت الشاي الأخضر عالرف التاني.
examples.trans: The green tea tin is on the second shelf.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian construct numeral for 'three' before plural nouns (تلت بيضات 'three eggs'), and also 'one third' (ساعة وتلت 'twenty past').

examples.trans: The recipe needs three large eggs.
It is twenty past three right now.

meanings.note: Standard word used in Jordanian Arabic for a part, portion, or section of something.

examples.trans: This is part of the problem.

examples.text: كل جزء من الخريطة مرسوم بدقة عجيبة.
examples.trans: Each part of the map is drawn with remarkable precision.

meanings.note: Used to address a group of people informally, like 'guys' or 'folks' ('ya jamaa'a').

examples.trans: Hey guys, let's go.

examples.text: يا جماعة الخير، التذوق رح يبلش هلق.
examples.trans: Everyone, the tasting is about to begin right now.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Go inside the house, the weather is cold.
The metal tin is hidden inside the cupboard.

meanings.note: Used warmly across ages in Jordan: يا حبيبي (to a boy/man, or as 'my goodness!') and يا حبيبتي (to a girl/woman).

examples.trans: Good morning, my dear.
A warm welcome to dear friends.

meanings.note: Seems to be a typo or portmanteau of 'habibti fi' (my love/dear in). Often used as a term of endearment.

examples.trans: My love is in the house.

examples.text: حبيبتي في المطبخ عم تجهز العسل واللوز.
examples.trans: My dear is in the kitchen preparing the honey and almonds.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Is anyone here?

examples.text: في حدا بعرف وين نحفظت الخريطة؟
examples.trans: Does anyone know where the map was stored?

meanings.note: Past tense verb in the second-person plural, indicating the action of digging.

examples.trans: Where did you (pl) dig the hole?

examples.text: وين حفرتوا تحت شجرة الزيزفون بالزبط؟
examples.trans: Where exactly did you dig under the linden tree?

meanings.note: Very common Levantine combination of the verb 'haka' (to speak/tell) and the preposition 'la' with a first-person suffix.

examples.trans: My friend told me the story.

examples.text: جدي حكالي قصة الخريطة واحنا صغار.
examples.trans: My grandfather told me the story of the map when we were young.

meanings.note: Form II verb used for the action of hiding something. Can be past tense 'they hid' or imperative 'hide (you pl)'.

examples.trans: They hid the money in the closet.

examples.text: خبوا البطاقة التالتة جوا غلاف الدفتر.
examples.trans: Hide the third card inside the notebook cover.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.text: افتح الخريطة على التلفون عشان ما نضيع.
examples.trans: Open the map on the phone so we don't get lost.
We followed the blue lines on the old map.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Can mean the metal lead, or bullets. Often used in 'qalam rSaaS' (pencil).

examples.trans: Write with a pencil so you can erase it.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بقلم رصاص خفيف جنب الزاوية.
examples.trans: The number is written in light pencil near the corner.

meanings.note: Everyday word for butter. Metaphorically means 'the essence' or 'bottom line'.

examples.trans: Give me the bottom line, what happened?

examples.text: دوبنا معلقة زبدة بلدية بالصينية قبل الخبز.
examples.trans: We melted a spoonful of local butter in the pan before baking.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: You are like my brother.

examples.text: ريحة الزيزفون زي ريحة الربيع بالقرية.
examples.trans: The scent of linden is like the scent of spring in the village.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of 'saa'il', meaning liquid.

examples.trans: This detergent is liquid, not powder.

examples.text: العسل السايل بنصب بسهولة على وجه الكيكة.
examples.trans: Runny honey pours easily over the top of the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Standard word for morning in both Classical and colloquial Arabic.

examples.trans: The weather is nice this morning.

examples.text: نسمات الصباح بالحديقة بتجيب ريحة الياسمين.
examples.trans: The morning breezes in the garden carry the scent of jasmine.

meanings.note: Dual form of ṣadīq (friend).

examples.trans: They are two friends from school days.

examples.text: مازن ورامي صديقين من أيام المدرسة.
examples.trans: Mazen and Rami have been two close friends since school days.

meanings.note: Used as an adjective for things related to summer, or as a noun for summer clothing.

examples.trans: We need to buy summer clothes.

examples.text: العسل الصيفي لونه أفتح ونكهته زهرية.
examples.trans: Summer honey is lighter in colour and has a floral flavour.

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.trans: The bread today is fresh.

examples.text: التوت اللي قطفناه اليوم طازة ومقرمش.
examples.trans: The berries we picked today are fresh and crisp.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective used for food (like meat) or soft materials.

examples.trans: The meat is tender and delicious.

examples.text: قطعنا قطعة كيكة طرية ودافية مع العسل.
examples.trans: We cut a soft, warm slice of cake with honey.

meanings.note: Used for a method of doing something, or sometimes a physical path.

examples.text: كل واحد إله طريقة في الشغل.
examples.trans: Everyone has their own way of working.

examples.text: هاي أسهل طريقة عشان توازن طعم الليمون.
examples.trans: This is the easiest way to balance the lemon flavour.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: The music volume is very high.

examples.text: الرف العالي بالخزانة عليه كتب جدتي.
examples.trans: The high shelf in the cupboard holds my grandmother's books.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: The car is at the door.

examples.text: التقينا عند برج الساعة الساعة عشرة.
examples.trans: We met by the clock tower at ten o'clock.

meanings.note: Can mean a unit of mass (gram) or deep love/infatuation depending on context.

examples.trans: I want a hundred grams of cheese.

examples.text: الوصفة بتحتاج ميتين غرام طحين وتمانين غرام زبدة.
examples.trans: The recipe needs two hundred grams of flour and eighty grams of butter.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Verbal noun referring to the act of reading or, more broadly, academic studying.

examples.trans: Reading is very beneficial for the mind.

examples.text: قراية الملاحظات المكتوبة بالهامش ساعدتنا كتير.
examples.trans: Reading the notes written in the margin helped us a great deal.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.trans: I will arrive very soon.

examples.text: سلمى رح ترجع قريب ومعها مرطبان العسل الجبلي.
examples.trans: Salma will be back soon bringing the jar of mountain honey.

meanings.note: Used to count items, or mean a portion, slice, or spare part.

examples.trans: I want a piece of cake please.

examples.text: كل واحد فينا أخذ قطعة صغيرة من كيكة اللوز.
examples.trans: Each one of us took a small piece of the almond cake.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person plural.

examples.trans: The boys were playing outside.

examples.text: الأولاد كانوا يدوروا عالعلبة الزرقا طول الصبح.
examples.trans: The children were looking for the blue tin all morning.

meanings.note: The word for book attached with the 1st person plural possessive suffix.

examples.trans: We got lost because we forgot our book at home.

examples.text: كتابنا فيه وصفات جدتي بالخط القديم والرسومات.
examples.trans: Our book contains my grandmother's recipes in old handwriting and drawings.

meanings.note: Refers to a literal treasure or something highly valued metaphorically.

examples.trans: They found an old treasure underground.

examples.text: الوصفات السرية اللي بالدفتر أغلى من أي كنز.
examples.trans: The secret recipes in the notebook are more precious than any treasure.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Used to give a reason, usually meaning 'because' broadly, or specifically 'because he/it is...'.

examples.trans: He didn't come because he is sick.

examples.text: ما فتحنا الشباك لأنه الهوا كان بارد كتير.
examples.trans: We did not open the window because the wind was very cold.

meanings.note: Used to mark the limit of a time period, distance, or extent in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: I will wait until you come.

examples.text: استنينا بالساحة لحد ما دقت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: We waited in the courtyard until the clock struck eight.

meanings.note: Used when dividing or cutting something into exactly two pieces.

examples.trans: Cut the apple into two halves.

examples.text: قسمنا رغيف الخبز السخن لنصين وتقاسمناه.
examples.trans: We split the warm loaf of bread into two halves and shared it.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.trans: The situation is perfect, don't worry.

examples.text: زينت سلمى وش الكيكة بشرايح لوز محمص.
examples.trans: Salma decorated the top of the cake with toasted almond slices.

meanings.note: Plural of 'līra'. In Jordan, people commonly refer to the Jordanian Dinar as a 'lira' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I only have five dinars left.

examples.text: دفعنا عشر ليرات حق المرطبانات الزجاج الجديدة.
examples.trans: We paid ten dinars for the new glass jars.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why were you late to work today?

examples.text: ليش الحبر على طرف الورقة مبين أغمق من النص؟
examples.trans: Why does the ink at the edge of the sheet look darker than the middle?

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Used when someone or something is jammed in a tight space or stuck in traffic. Also used for needing to go to the bathroom urgently.

examples.trans: The car was stuck in traffic for an hour.

examples.text: الكرت كان محشور بين الغلاف الخشبي والورقة الأولى.
examples.trans: The card was wedged between the wooden cover and the first page.

meanings.note: Something placed underground or covered heavily. Can also refer to a traditional rice and meat dish.

examples.trans: The treasure is buried underground.

examples.text: الصندوق النحاس كان مدفون تحت بلاطة الساحة.
examples.trans: The brass chest was buried under a courtyard paving stone.

meanings.note: Used to describe a neat person, a well-organized room, or generally something of high quality (e.g. 'a nice car').

examples.trans: Working with him is very neat and well-organized.

examples.text: خطها مرتب وواضح كتير حتى عالورق الصغير.
examples.trans: Her handwriting is very neat and clear even on small paper.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for tearing or ripping something apart.

examples.trans: He tore the paper and threw it in the trash.

examples.text: طارق مزع طرف المغلف بحذر عشان ما يخرب الختم.
examples.trans: Tariq tore the edge of the envelope carefully so as not to ruin the seal.

meanings.note: Used for things like coffee, spices, or meat.

examples.trans: I want freshly ground coffee.

examples.text: ضفنا نص معلقة هيل مطحون ناعم عالقهوة.
examples.trans: We added half a spoonful of finely ground cardamom to the coffee.

meanings.note: Used for things that are cut or split into parts.

examples.trans: The cake is divided into two halves.

examples.text: الورقة مقسومة بخط رصاص إلى تلات أقسام متساوية.
examples.trans: The sheet is divided by a pencil line into three equal sections.

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: The name is written on the board.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بخط صغير تحت الختم الأحمر.
examples.trans: The number is written in small handwriting beneath the red seal.

meanings.note: Feminine form of maktub, used as an adjective for feminine nouns.

examples.trans: The message is written in nice handwriting.

examples.text: الوصفة الأصلية مكتوبة على ضهر كرت التذوق.
examples.trans: The original recipe is written on the back of the tasting card.

meanings.note: Used for remarks, annotations, or paying attention to details.

examples.trans: I have a small note on the work.

examples.text: سجلنا ملاحظة صغيرة عن نكهة قشر البرتقال.
examples.trans: We jotted down a short note about the orange peel flavour.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of the dual form for 100.

examples.trans: I only have two hundred dinars.

examples.text: الوصفة بتحتاج ميتين غرام طحين منخول ومية غرام سكر.
examples.trans: The recipe needs two hundred grams of sifted flour and a hundred grams of sugar.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who rang the bell?

examples.text: مين كتب هاي الملاحظة عالورقة بالحبر الأزرق؟
examples.trans: Who wrote this note on the paper in blue ink?

meanings.note: Most common verb for searching ('ndawwir 'ala') or turning something around.

examples.trans: We have been looking for you for an hour.

examples.text: خلينا ندور بالرفوف التحتانية بلكي نلاقي الدفتر.
examples.trans: Let us look through the bottom shelves; maybe we will find the notebook.

meanings.note: Noun 'half' with the feminine 3rd person singular pronoun suffix.

examples.trans: I ate half of it and left the rest.

examples.text: قرأنا نصها والباقي رح نكمله بكرة بالمكتبة.
examples.trans: We read half of it and the rest we will finish tomorrow in the library.

meanings.note: First person plural present verb.

examples.trans: Maybe we will find a solution to the problem.

examples.text: بلكي نلاقي الحل بسرعة لما نقرأ البطاقات بالترتيب.
examples.trans: Maybe we will find the answer quickly when we read the cards in order.

meanings.note: Demonstrative phrase for a book.

examples.trans: This book is very useful for the exam.

examples.text: استعرت هالكتاب من مكتبة الجامعة عشان البحث.
examples.trans: I borrowed this book from the university library for the research paper.

meanings.note: Points out a written piece.

examples.trans: This text is long and needs time to read.

examples.text: قرأنا هالنص القصير بالصف وجاوبنا على كل الأسئلة.
examples.trans: We read this short passage in class and answered all the questions.

meanings.note: Contracted phrase pointing out a card or ticket.

examples.trans: Take this card so you can enter.

examples.text: سجل اسمك على هبطاقة وحطها بالصندوق.
examples.trans: Write your name on this card and drop it in the box.

meanings.note: Usually refers to mobile network coverage.

examples.trans: The internet is excellent and the coverage is strong here.

examples.text: سافرت عالصحرا والتغطية انقطعت نص الطريق.
examples.trans: I drove out to the desert and the cell coverage dropped halfway there.

meanings.note: Refers to the nut, also used metaphorically for something excellent.

examples.trans: We ate fruits and green almonds.

examples.text: زينت أمي المقلوبة بالصنوبر واللوز المحمص.
examples.trans: My mom garnished the maqluba with pine nuts and toasted almonds.

meanings.note: Refers to flapping wings or hovering. The spelling appears to be a colloquial variant or typo for بيرفرف.

examples.trans: The bird is flying and fluttering its wings.

examples.text: شوف العلم كيف مرفوع فوق السطح وبيرفوف بالهوا.
examples.trans: Look how the flag is raised on the roof and fluttering in the breeze.

meanings.note: Refers to mulberries or any kind of berries.

examples.trans: We brought strawberries and berries from the market.

examples.text: عملت ماما مربى مشمش وتوت للفطور بالشتوية.
examples.trans: Mom made apricot and mulberry jam for breakfast during the winter.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: The car is behind the house.

examples.text: الحديقة موجودة ورا المبنى بعيدة عن عجقة الشارع.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the building, away from the street traffic.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Used for both a doctor's prescription and a cooking recipe.

examples.trans: The doctor gave me the medicine prescription.

examples.text: جربت وصفة الكعك تبعت خالتي وطلعت بتشهي.
examples.trans: I tried my aunt's cookie recipe and it turned out mouthwatering.

meanings.note: Past tense verb combined with 'and', directed at a group.

examples.trans: Did you finish the work and go out early?

examples.text: سافرتوا عالعقبة وطلعتوا بالقارب بالبحر الأحمر؟
examples.trans: Did you travel to Aqaba and go out on the boat in the Red Sea?

meanings.note: General term for time or duration.

examples.trans: I don't have time to go out today.

examples.text: بياخد الطريق من عمان لعجلون تقريباً وقت ساعة.
examples.trans: The road from Amman to Ajloun takes roughly an hour of time.

meanings.note: Past tense, second person feminine singular.

examples.trans: Why did you stop in the middle of the road?

examples.text: ليش وقفتي السيارة بعيد عن المدخل رغم إنه فاضي؟
examples.trans: Why did you park the car far from the entrance even though it's empty?

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Not even one of them came.

examples.text: سألت الكل بس ولا حدا بيعرف وين حطوا المفتاح.
examples.trans: I asked everyone, yet not a single person knows where they put the key.

meanings.note: Refers to half of a feminine object or quantity.

examples.text: أكلت التفاحة ونصها الثاني لسه موجود.
examples.trans: I ate the apple and the other half is still there.

examples.text: قرأت القصة ونصها التاني خليته لقبل النوم.
examples.trans: I read the story and left the second half of it for bedtime.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where are you going?

examples.text: وين حطيت مفاتيح السيارة بعد ما رجعت من الشغل؟
examples.trans: Where did you put the car keys after you got back from work?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial verb for eating.

examples.trans: He wants to eat an apple.

examples.text: أخي الصغير ما بحب يوكل خضار مسلوقة بدون ليمون.
examples.trans: My little brother doesn't like to eat boiled vegetables without lemon.
